findings.title: Client-sent x-vercel-isr header reopens path-override bypass on _render
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone can reopen the untrusted path override that #15959 closed. They only need to add the plain request header `x-vercel-isr: 1` and `?x_astro_path=<target>` to a request that lands on the regular `_render` function. `_render` and `_isr` are built from the same entryFile, and nothing ties the new branch to the ISR function or to a secret. So a request routed as `/api/public` renders `/api/private`, which defeats Vercel-side path controls (vercel.json rules, firewall and protection keyed on the public path). I reproduced this in-process against the already-built `_render` fixture. The one thing I could not check offline is whether Vercel's edge strips a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` header. Restricting the branch to the ISR function (for example by also requiring the invoked pathname to be `/_isr`, or by baking an `isIsr` flag into the ISR build) keeps ISR working and closes the header-only bypass.
findings.suggested_fix: Honor the query param only when the ISR function itself is being invoked, e.g. `} else if (url.pathname === '/_isr' && request.headers.get('x-vercel-isr') === '1') {` (assumes Vercel invokes the ISR function with pathname `/_isr`, which the ISR_PATH comment in index.ts implies), or preferably emit a build-time flag for the `_isr` function (a separate entry or virtual config value) so `_render` never honors `x_astro_path`. Add a case to test/path-override-security.test.js: `_render.fetch(new Request('https://example.com/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private', { headers: { 'x-vercel-isr': '1' } }))` must return id 'public'.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:452,474 -- builder.buildServerlessFolder(entryFile, NODE_PATH, ...) and builder.buildISRFolder(entryFile, '_isr', ...) share the same entry, so _render contains the new branch (confirmed in built chunk entrypoint_Bvfzwt1s.mjs:13997)

In-process repro (PRERENDER=true) against test/fixtures/serverless-with-dynamic-routes _render: Request('https://example.com/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private') -> {"id":"public"}; same request with header x-vercel-isr: 1 -> {"id":"private"}; also '/nonexistent?x_astro_path=/api/private' + header -> 200 {"id":"private"}

packages/integrations/vercel/test/path-override-security.test.js asserts exactly this bypass is closed ('ignores untrusted x_astro_path query param on _render') but does not send x-vercel-isr, so the suite stays green
Platform assumption (unverifiable offline): Vercel does not strip or overwrite a client-supplied x-vercel-isr request header before invoking a non-prerender function

findings.title: Direct /_isr?x_astro_path=<excluded route> renders ISR-excluded routes and skips edge middleware
findings.why_it_matters: The ISR function now renders whatever path is in `x_astro_path` without checking that the path is an ISR route. If a client can call `/_isr?x_astro_path=/two` directly (the ISR fixture's routes start with `handle: filesystem`, and Vercel presumably sets x-vercel-isr on every invocation of the prerender function), routes that were explicitly excluded from ISR get rendered by the ISR function and cached for `expiration` seconds under that key. With middlewareMode 'edge', those excluded routes are normally reached only through `_middleware`, so this path skips the edge middleware that guards them. This is platform-dependent: I could not confirm offline that `/_isr` is directly reachable or that the header is set on direct hits.
findings.suggested_fix: In the ISR branch, after rewriting, reject the override when the matched route is excluded from ISR or is not an ISR route (e.g. bake the ISR-excluded route patterns into the _isr function config at build time and return 404 when app.match on realPath hits one), assuming ISR routes are exactly the non-excluded, non-prerendered routes emitted with dest ISR_PATH in index.ts.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:476-490 -- only non-excluded routes get dest ISR_PATH; excluded ones go to `_middlewareEntryPoint ? MIDDLEWARE_PATH : NODE_PATH`
test/fixtures/isr/.vercel/output/config.json -- routes begin with { "handle": "filesystem" }, so the _isr function path may be matched directly

residual_risks: Whether Vercel strips or overwrites client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` headers at the edge is undocumented and could not be verified offline. The whole trust model of this fix depends on it, and the PR gives no evidence either way.
testing_gaps: path-override-security.test.js has no case that sends `x-vercel-isr: 1` to `_render` with `?x_astro_path=`, and nothing tests that `_isr` still honors the param. The ISR regression this PR fixes could come back unnoticed, and so could the bypass it risks reopening.
